scope: new read-only data-collection master ledger and drift report; QMD delivery entry point, R boundary helper, and offline test suites

key_findings: R helper passed NULL for registry/external paths, silently disabling external inventory while the QMD displayed those paths as inputs
timer-scheduled services without their own wants link were not counted as scheduled
repository unit definitions were mixed into the host inventory, masking repo_unit_not_scheduled
a live store beside its .bak backup was wrongly classified retired; a prefix glob accepted unrelated -other.bak names
registry-declared store references were never reconciled with filesystem evidence
unavailable requested inputs were indistinguishable from genuinely empty inputs
wants detection used a hard-coded target list and accepted dangling symlinks
unit paths with systemd specifiers or bare ~ were mishandled
collectors matched units by script basename, allowing a foreign same-named script to mark a collector running
retirement evidence accepted any schema containing 'retirement'
invalid UTF-8 registry bytes raised instead of recording an unreadable input
the R boundary coerced values instead of validating declared column types
the R boundary tests read live data and converted all errors to skips
store_stale_days was accepted but ignored
R host unit defaults still included the repository ops/systemd/user directory
a scheduled timer with an explicit Unit= also scheduled the same-basename service
the R boundary still coerced character/integer/numeric values
provenance recorded paths, not input evidence identities
timestamp parsing ignored timezone offsets
collection_ledger_run never returned repo_units
nested store state was not extracted into the store_state column
evidence digests omitted store observations, so a newly available store left the digest unchanged
wants-directory identity was lost, so moving an unchanged link between target directories produced the same digest
resolutions: moved evidence binding into the authoritative Python ledger as a bounded observation manifest (plan file hash, unit files and wants links by absolute path, registry file hashes, external-root direct children, collector store observations)
removed the unbounded R-side directory digesting
resolve Python module defaults instead of passing NULL from R, and default host unit dirs to the host only
count timer-scheduled services, honoring an explicit Unit= without also scheduling the basename service
keep the repository unit inventory separate from the host inventory and reconcile by name
retire a store only when the registered file is absent and an exact <name><marker> sibling exists
reconcile registry-declared stores with filesystem availability and require a validated retirement schema
distinguish unavailable inputs (available/unavailable states and findings) from empty results
discover *.target.wants directories and reject dangling links
expand supported systemd specifiers and treat unresolved paths as unknown, not absent
match collectors by resolved code identity rather than script basename
catch invalid UTF-8 as an unreadable registry input
validate declared R column types and reject incompatible source values while preserving typed empties
make R boundary tests deterministic on temp fixtures with no catch-all error-to-skip
bind provenance to a bounded input observation manifest computed by the Python ledger
honor the store_stale_days parameter through to store classification
return repo_units and extract nested store state into the collector table

reviewed_qmd_note: The recorded quarto/collection_ledger.qmd hash is the revision reviewed in round 3; the acceptance section appended to the document afterwards is a review record only and does not change the reviewed implementation.
limitations: Read-only file-evidence classification; live systemctl runtime state is not queried ('running' means scheduled, not last-run-successful)
Evidence digests are bounded observation manifests (file hashes, direct-child metadata, store observations), not recursive hashes of the data tree
The host unit directory, external registry and external data root are out-of-repository inputs; cross-host replay requires the same host unit directory and an equivalent external-disk snapshot
An unmounted external disk yields 'unavailable' inputs with findings, not missing objects
No CI configuration was added and no CI status is claimed as acceptance
